non_claims: The C-glycosylation position (6-C versus 8-C) is not claimed; the published intensity-ratio criteria for it depend on collision energy and instrument
Sugar identity (hexose versus pentose), unit counts and the aglycone formula come from the chosen hypothesis and are not claimed

The aglycone skeleton rests on the precondition's flavonoid formula list, which isobaric non-flavonoid aglycones can share (for example aloe-emodin anthrone, C15H12O4, in aloin); anthrone C-glycosides are listed as a competitor

notes: Deprotonated mono-C-glycosyl flavonoids give the aglycone+41 and +71 ions of the C-sugar (losses of 120 and 90 for a hexose, 90 and 60 for a pentose) while the even and radical aglycone ions stay weak.

competitors.note: Flavonoid O-glycosides share compositions with C-glycosides (apigenin 7-O-glucoside and vitexin are both C21H20O10) and lose whole sugars to a strong Y0.
Anthrone C-glycosides (aloin C21H22O9, 10-hydroxyaloin C21H22O10) have the compositions of C15H12O4 and C15H12O5 hexoside hypotheses, so their C-glucose cross-ring targets coincide with x02 and x03.

terms.note: [A-H+C2H2O]- (A+41), the 0,2X ion of the C-sugar: [M-H]- minus C4H8O4 (120) for Hex or C3H6O3 (90) for Pen; aglycone-relative, so an adduct hypothesis cannot meet it by adduct loss
[A-H+C3H4O2]- (A+71), the 0,3X ion of the C-sugar: [M-H]- minus C3H6O3 (90) for Hex or C2H4O2 (60) for Pen; aglycone-relative, so an adduct hypothesis cannot meet it by adduct loss
Y0 [aglycone-H]-: base peak of O-glycosides, weak or absent for C-glycosides
Radical Y0 [aglycone-2H]-., weak for flavone C-glucosides
